cards.text: At that time, Abimelech, king of Gerar (Genesis 20:2), comes to Abraham with Phicol, the commander of his army. A king AND his army commander, together? Friend, when two bosses walk up to your desk at the same time, you check your pulse.

cards.question: Abimelech opens with something he's noticed about Abraham. What does he say?

answers.text: God is with him in all he does
His flocks grow bigger every year

cards.text: Then Abimelech gets to the point: he wants Abraham to swear an oath, right there before God. Friend, nobody brings the commander of his ARMY along for a pinky promise.

cards.question: What does Abimelech want Abraham to swear before God?

answers.text: He won't deal falsely with him or his family
He will give the king half of his flocks
He will leave the king's land by spring

cards.question: Abimelech also asks Abraham to show him and the country the same kindness Abimelech has shown Abraham.
Abraham tells Abimelech he needs time to think it over before he swears anything.

cards.text: Abraham says, “I swear it.” Three words, done, faster than I say yes to a cookie fresh off the rack. But then Abraham's got a complaint of his own, and he takes it straight to the king.

cards.question: What is Abraham's complaint to Abimelech about?

answers.text: A well the king's servants seized
Sheep stolen out of his flock
A field the king's army burned

cards.question: Abimelech says he knew all about the well and was waiting for Abraham to bring it up.

cards.text: Abimelech says he has no idea who did it, and since Abraham never told him, today's the first he's hearing of it. Friend, that's me in every group chat: "Wait. WHEN did this happen?"

cards.question: So Abraham brings Abimelech ___ and ___, and the two men make a covenant.

cards.text: Covenant made. Then Abraham separates seven ewe lambs from the flock and sets them off by themselves, and I bet Abimelech's standing there like, "Uh. What are THOSE for?"

cards.question: Abimelech asks Abraham why he set apart the seven ewe lambs. What does Abraham say the seven ewe lambs are?

answers.text: His witness that he dug the well
A gift for the king's children
An offering for a safe journey

cards.question: The place where Abraham and Abimelech settled things over the well gets a name: Beersheba. Why does it get that name?

answers.text: The two men swore an oath there

cards.text: Abimelech and Phicol head back to the land of the Philistines, and Abraham plants a tamarisk tree in Beersheba. Most of us walk out of a big meeting and check our phones, but Abraham? Abraham grabs a SHOVEL.

cards.question: There in Beersheba, what else does Abraham do?

answers.text: He calls on the name of the LORD
He builds a house for Sarah
He digs a second well nearby

cards.question: Abraham stays in the land of the Philistines for a long time.

cards.text: Don't take your apron off yet, friend. Abraham's story still has a few batches in it.

findings.problem: The joke 'nobody brings the commander of his ARMY along for a pinky promise' gives Abimelech a motive for bringing Phicol, as a show of force or seriousness. Genesis 21:22-23 never says why Phicol came. Card 1's joke about checking your pulse already leans the same way, so this card states the motive outright.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Abraham says, “I swear it.”' / 'Three words, done, faster than I say yes to a cookie fresh off the rack.' / 'But then Abraham's got a complaint of his own…' It isn't the opening card, so it can have at most two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The two right words, sheep and cattle, are locked to blanks 1 and 2. A baker who picks 'cattle' for the first blank and 'sheep' for the second has the same meaning but would be marked wrong. The BSB order is 'sheep and cattle', but the blank tests meaning, and the order carries none here.
findings.question: When a two-blank card's right words could go in either order without changing the meaning, should either order count as right, should the blanks be reworded so each word has only one place, or should the card use one blank instead?
